integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, documentary, a medium shot at a shallow indoor teaching pool in flat overhead light, a child in a yellow swim cap and orange armbands standing chest-deep at the edge with both hands on the tiled lip. The camera tilts up with small amplitude at slow speed from the rippling water surface to the coach crouched at the pool edge above the child, a woman in a navy tracksuit with a whistle on a cord, on-screen, thirties, with a bright, carrying soprano and a brisk delivery (S1). She taps two fingers under her own chin, looks straight at the child, and says to her: <d>[French] Regarde-moi, pas l'eau.</d> Her lips close into a smile as the child lifts her chin from the water, laughs, and kicks a spray of water against the tiles.

overall_soundscape: Water laps and slaps against tiled pool walls under a bright echoing hall reverb with a distant filter pump. A child's laugh rings out and bounces off the ceiling, followed by a splash of kicked water and the squeak of a rubber sole on wet tile.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, a medium shot frames a late-night beef-noodle counter from the street side, a steel stockpot steaming under a bare bulb and a row of red plastic stools along the tiled front. Above the serving hatch a neon sign reading "老张牛肉面" glows in red tube script, mounted flush to the tiled lintel and centred over the hatch. A small radio on the shelf behind the counter plays a Cantonese pop song, a bright synth-backed ballad at a steady mid-tempo, thin and tinny through its single speaker. The camera zooms out with small amplitude at slow speed, opening the frame from the sign to the whole counter. A customer in a grey raincoat, on-screen, thirties, with a low, even tenor and a quick delivery (S1), steps up to the hatch, holds up two fingers toward the cook, and says: <d>[Chinese] 两碗牛肉面，一碗不要辣。</d> He closes his mouth and lowers his hand to the counter edge. The cook in a white apron behind the stockpot nods once, lifts a ladle, and produces no vocal sound.

overall_soundscape: A stockpot simmers steadily under the hum of a neon transformer. A ladle knocks against steel, a coat sleeve brushes the counter edge, and traffic passes wet and distant on the street behind.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Watercolor, a soft-edged painted look with visible paper grain and bleeding edges, a medium shot frames the front window of a village post office under falling snow, a brass letter slot at the left of frame and a low stone step below the glass. A hand-lettered card propped inside the window reads "CLOSED FOR STOCKTAKING" in uneven black capitals on cream board. The camera holds a static shot for the whole take. Snow gathers along the bottom rail of the window and thickens on the stone step below. A tabby cat sits on the inner sill behind the glass, blinks once, folds its paws, and produces no vocal sound. An unseen hand inside pushes a single envelope out through the letter slot. It tips over the lip and settles face down on the step as the snowfall continues.

overall_soundscape: Muffled snowfall softens a narrow lane and a faint creak works through the wooden window frame. The letter slot flaps once and the envelope lands on the stone step with a small dry slap.

non_diegetic_music: Two alternating celesta notes at a slow tempo, joined by a sustained low string that swells briefly and thins away before the final frame.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, the shot is the runner's own point of view (POV) crossing a gravel rooftop at dusk, gloved hands pumping in and out of the bottom of frame, a low brick parapet ahead and the lit windows of the next building beyond it. The camera shakes strongly with every stride as the gravel rushes underfoot and the parapet grows across the frame. From the stairwell door behind, a woman, off-screen, thirties, with a sharp, carrying alto and a fast clipped delivery (S1), shouts: <d>[English] Left, go left!</d> The gloved hands swing toward the left corner of the parapet as her voice stops. [Shot 2] The shot transitions to a wide shot from the neighbouring roof, the runner, on-screen, in a dark hooded jacket and gloves, sprinting the last strides along the parapet line with the city skyline behind. The camera pulls out with large amplitude at fast speed as the runner plants one foot on the brick, vaults the gap with arms spread, and lands hard on the gravel of the near roof, skidding to a crouch with both hands down. The runner's chest heaves and no words are spoken.

overall_soundscape: Gravel crunches in fast strides under a hard, ragged panting that carries through both shots. Wind rushes past on the rooftop, a jacket zip rattles, and the landing hits with a heavy scrape of boots and gloves on loose stone over distant traffic below.

non_diegetic_music: A dry kick-and-snare pattern at a fast tempo, joined by a low pulsing synth bass that rises in volume toward the vault and cuts to a single sustained hit on the landing.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Vintage film, 16mm grain with warm faded colour and soft halation around the lights, a medium shot frames a cinema box-office booth from the pavement side, a curved glass window with a brass coin dish and a red-lettered board above it reading "TONIGHT ONLY 7:30". A cashier behind the glass, on-screen, sixties, with a flat, papery contralto (S1), sits with a roll of tickets under one hand; a teenage customer at the window, on-screen, with a thin, hurried tenor (S2), leans toward the dish holding a folded note. The camera tilts down with small amplitude at slow speed from the lettered board to the coin dish. The cashier (S1) taps the glass beside her and says: <d>[English] Seven thirty, nothing after.</d> She closes her lips. The customer (S2) slides the note and two coins into the dish and answers: <d>[English] Two, back row.</d> His lips settle closed. The cashier (S1) tears two tickets from the roll and adds: <d>[English] Back row is gone, love.</d> Her lips close as she pushes the tickets across the brass.

overall_soundscape: Street ambience carries under the low buzz of a neon transformer above the booth. Coins ring in a brass dish, paper tickets tear from a roll, and a shoe scuffs on wet pavement.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, a medium-wide shot frames a radio-drama studio with acoustic panels on the walls, three actors standing at a row of microphones on boom stands, and a foley table stacked with props at the left of frame. Above the studio door an illuminated sign reading "ON AIR" glows in red block capitals on a white panel, mounted high on the wall at the top left of frame. A foley artist in a grey cardigan walks from the door to her table carrying a pair of leather shoes, on-screen, and produces no vocal sound. The camera follows her as a tracking shot with small amplitude at slow speed until she sets the shoes on a square of gravel. An older actor in a waistcoat at the first microphone, on-screen, sixties, with a deep, resonant bass and a slow delivery (S1), reads from his script toward the actress beside him: <d>[English] Someone is on the stairs.</d> His lips close as he lowers the page. The actress at the second microphone in a green scarf, on-screen, forties, with a warm, husky alto and a quick delivery (S2), leans in and answers him: <d>[English] Then put out the lamp.</d> Her mouth closes and the foley artist walks the shoes across the gravel in slow steps. [Shot 2] The camera cuts to a close shot of the third actor at the last microphone, a young man in headphones, on-screen, twenties, with a light, breathy tenor and a hesitant delivery (S3), a burned-in subtitle in white sans-serif lettering sitting in the lower third of frame reading "I can hear him breathing." The camera holds a static shot. He grips the script with both hands, looks toward the actress at the second microphone, and whispers: <d>[English] I can hear him breathing.</d><|caption_start|>I can hear him breathing.<|caption_end|> His lips close and he holds still as the foley steps stop on the gravel.

overall_soundscape: A close, padded studio room tone carries under the soft hum of a monitor speaker. Leather shoes press slowly into a tray of gravel, script pages turn, a boom stand creaks, and a chair castor rolls once across carpet.

non_diegetic_music: A low bowed double bass at a slow tempo holds a single sustained note, joined by a sparse pizzicato figure that enters at the cut and stops on the final frame.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, documentary, a wide shot frames a two-lane desert highway at midday, heat shimmer flattening the ridge behind and a yellow road roller parked with its engine idling at the edge of the fresh asphalt. A crew supervisor in a high-visibility vest and a wide-brimmed hat, on-screen, fifties, with a dry, carrying alto and an unhurried delivery (S1), stands at the centre line holding a clipboard, and a younger crew member in the same vest, on-screen, mid-twenties, with a light, slightly nasal tenor (S2), kneels over a seam of fresh asphalt at the right of frame. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed along the centre line toward the two of them. [Shot 2] The camera cuts to a medium shot of the pair at the seam, the roller's drum filling the left edge. The supervisor (S1) taps the clipboard against her thigh and says: <d>[English] Give it another pass before the sun drops.</d> Her voice continues seamlessly across the cut. [Shot 3] The shot cuts to a low close shot of the parked roller's drum resting against the seam, and the supervisor's last words carry over from the previous shot and remain audible across the transition. The camera holds a static shot on the drum. The younger crew member (S2) leans into frame above the drum and answers: <d>[English] Two more and it's flat.</d> He closes his mouth and steps back onto the gravel.

overall_soundscape: A diesel engine idles under a steady wash of hot wind across open ground. Gravel shifts under boots, the idling roller's steel drum hums against fresh asphalt with a low hiss, and a clipboard taps twice against fabric.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, a vintage slapstick comedy style captures an outdoor staircase mishap across the fourteen-second take, laundry flapping overhead beside a painted enamel street sign reading "HIGH STREET STAIRS". Two bumbling moving men in ill-fitting bowler hats and oversized work dungarees struggle to carry a massive upright wooden piano down the narrow steps. The lead mover at the lower end, on-screen, thirties, with a high, squeaky tenor and a panicked delivery (S1), strains under the crushing weight. A bystander walking a tiny poodle at the top landing pauses to watch and produces no vocal sound. The lead mover (S1) looks up the steps toward his partner and yelps: <d>[English] Hold the handbrake rope, Barnaby, it's slipping through my fingers!</d> His mouth flies open in theatrical terror, then snaps into an aghast round circle as his heels skid on the concrete. The camera pedestals down with small amplitude at slow speed following the groaning piano. [Shot 2] The shot transitions to a medium shot of his heavyset partner at the top of the stairs, on-screen, forties, with a deep, slow-witted baritone and a bewildered delivery (S2), holding a frayed hemp rope that suddenly snaps in two with a puff of dust. The partner (S2) stares at the broken rope end, looks down toward his partner, and mutters: <d>[English] Well, look on the bright side, it's much lighter now.</d> His lips close into a blank, deadpan expression and his bowler hat slips comically over his eyebrows. The camera zooms in with small amplitude at fast speed on his vacant expression. [Shot 3] The shot changes to a wide three-shot from the bottom of the long stairs as the lead mover dives aside onto the banister and the upright piano careens uncontrollably down the concrete steps like a toboggan, striking all its internal strings with a cacophony of musical chords before crashing into an empty soft fruit cart at the curb in an explosion of flying oranges. The camera holds a static shot as both movers slide down the banister rails in pursuit.

overall_soundscape: Heavy wooden piano casters rumble and bounce violently down concrete stairs under a reverberant outdoor alley acoustic. A thick hemp rope snaps with a sharp crack, piano keys and internal strings chime in chaotic dissonance, and crates of fresh oranges crash open.

non_diegetic_music: An uproarious silent film ragtime piano score at a fast tempo, featuring lightning-fast stride piano bass, dizzying chromatic treble scales, and a comical trombone slide whistle that accents the piano crash.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, a sleek cinematic modern music video in a minimalist rehearsal studio bathed in crisp ice-blue rim lighting unfolds across the fourteen-second take, back-wall mirrors reflecting synchronized movement beneath an illuminated wall graphic reading "STUDIO ZERO". A K-pop lead vocalist in a monochrome cropped street-dance jacket, on-screen, twenties, with a bright, crystalline soprano and an energetic rhythm (S1), executes a sharp isolation dance routine before a centered standing microphone. Four backup dancers in dark cargo joggers hold a frozen freeze pose at the mirrored corner and produce no vocal sound. The camera pans right with small amplitude at fast speed across the dance line as the singer steps forward and sings: <|lyrics_start|><d>[Korean] 심장이 뛰는 소리를 들어봐.</d><|lyrics_end|> Her lips seal into a sharp, poised pout and her head snaps to the camera angle. [Shot 2] The shot switches to a tight medium close shot of the vocalist from a low perspective, vertical LED light bars strobing in white and violet behind her. The singer (S1) performs a crisp hand-tutting combination, smiles into the lens, and delivers the punchy hook: <|lyrics_start|><d>[English] Never stop the beat, light up the night!</d><|lyrics_end|> Her mouth firmly closes on the final syllable and her jaw locks into a confident posture. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at fast speed toward her eyes. [Shot 3] The camera cuts to a wide center-stage shot framing the singer dropping into a synchronized floor spin alongside the four backup dancers, silhouetted against the glowing back wall. The camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed, then holds a static shot as the performers freeze in a sharp final silhouette formation.

overall_soundscape: Clean sneaker soles squeak crisply against polished polyurethane flooring during sudden dance pivots. Fabric swishes sharply on arm movements, followed by controlled panting breaths and the click of light bar relays.

non_diegetic_music: A high-octane electronic K-pop dance track at a fast tempo, powered by hard-hitting trap 808 sub-bass, snappy synth claps, arpeggiated supersaw chords, and aggressive vocal stutter chops that end on an abrupt downbeat.
